prompt:
Use case: background-extraction
Asset type: utility ALPHA MASK for a game brightness overlay, exact 2172x724 pixels, 3:1 landscape, transparent PNG.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and exact alignment reference (space panorama). Input image 2 is an ANNOTATION REFERENCE: green strokes roughly indicate the luminous curving dust filaments to select. Do not include the green strokes themselves.
Create ONLY a smooth soft WHITE alpha mask selecting the diffuse brighter curving nebula/dust bands of image 1. Preserve their exact layout/position across the full canvas. Main sweeping band travels from left edge at about y=60 percent down into a trough at x=25 percent/y=88 percent, curves up through x=48 percent/y=60 percent and into the moon surroundings at x=65 percent/y=35 percent, then has a right branch reaching right edge around y=45 percent. Additional faint upper branch curves down from x=57 percent/y=0 toward x=65 percent/y=35 percent. White/soft-opacity band widths around 5-10 percent of height, gently feathered edges. The mask should follow the nebula filaments, not thin lightning bolts.
EVERYTHING ELSE must be actual transparency: all empty black space, all individual stars, the entire rocky moon silhouette and all small rocky bodies. Especially exclude the moon itself: no mask at x=67..82 percent y=15..69 percent except surrounding nebula outside its silhouette. The output must have no visible image colours, no black background, no stars, no planet, no new detail, no text and no green marks. It is just soft white selection bands on transparent background, to be composited precisely over the original panorama by runtime code. Keep canvas dimensions and geometry unchanged.
usage: Alpha selection only. Runtime adds a masked copy of the original panorama; the original artwork is unchanged.
